t: This is the Church of St Anselm on Kennington Road, a Grade II listed building from 1932 to 33. It's famously described as barn-like. It stands on the foundations of an earlier church whose building was interrupted by the First World War. It was designed by Stanley Davenport Adshead and Stanley Ramsey, who were partners from 1911 to 1931. Adshead was invited that year to design the Duchy of Cornwall Estate in Kennington, and brought Ramsey into the partnership. The pair also designed the brass box for the Princess Mary Christmas gift.
